facts.fact_text: The applicants are members of EĞİTİM-SEN (Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası – The Education Workers' Trade Union).
EĞİTİM-SEN (Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası – The Education Workers' Trade Union) is a trade union.

EĞİTİM-SEN (Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası – The Education Workers' Trade Union) is a member of KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions).
In 2001 the Turkish Parliament prepared a draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions.

While the draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions was being discussed in the Turkish Parliament, KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) decided to organise meetings in Ankara to protest the bill.

The aim of the meetings organised by KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) was to draw public attention to the draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions.

The aim of the meetings organised by KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) was to achieve the withdrawal of the draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions.

In the view of KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions), the draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions did not meet international standards.

On 7 June 2001, Şehrinaz Artar was examined by a doctor from the Hacettepe University Hospital.
On 7 June 2001, Ömer Buzludağ was examined by a doctor from the Hacettepe University Hospital.
The doctor from the Hacettepe University Hospital noted an ecchymosis of 2x2 cm on the left eyebrow of Şehrinaz Artar.
The doctor from the Hacettepe University Hospital noted an abrasion of 3 cm on the right eyebrow of Ömer Buzludağ.
On 25 June 2001, Arzu Doğan was examined by a forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed an ecchymosis on the lip of Arzu Doğan.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed a hyperaemic graze on the left wrist of Arzu Doğan.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed superficial abrasions on the right wrist of Arzu Doğan.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed superficial abrasions on the right arm of Arzu Doğan.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute concluded that the injuries rendered Arzu Doğan unfit for work for one day.
On 25 June 2001, Tacettin Yağdıran was examined by a forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed a sutured injury on the occipital lobe of the head of Tacettin Yağdıran.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed a haematoma under the sutured injury on the occipital lobe of the head of Tacettin Yağdıran.
The forensic medical expert from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute considered that the injuries of Tacettin Yağdıran rendered him unfit for work for seven days.
On 25 June 2001, Elif Akgül was examined by a doctor from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute.
The doctor from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed abrasions on the skin on the left scapula of Elif Akgül.
The doctor from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed abrasions on the skin on the back of Elif Akgül.
The doctor from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute observed a haematoma of 2x2 cm on the right frontal lobe of Elif Akgül.
The doctor from the Ankara Forensic Medicine Institute concluded that the injuries rendered Elif Akgül unfit for work for five days.
On 18 December 2000, the Governorship of Ankara issued a circular providing guidelines on meetings and demonstrations organised in the city of Ankara.
The circular issued by the Governorship of Ankara on 18 December 2000 was issued in accordance with the Law on Meetings and Demonstration Marches (Law no. 2911).

According to the circular issued by the Governorship of Ankara on 18 December 2000, the meeting place chosen by KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) was not among the permitted areas.

At the material time, section 10 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) required that, in order for a meeting to take place, the governor's office or authorities of the district in which the demonstration is planned must be informed during opening hours and at least seventy-two hours prior to the meeting.

At the material time, section 10 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) required that the notification to the governor's office or district authorities must be by a notice containing the signature of all the members of the organising board.
Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibited demonstrations and processions on public streets.
Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibited demonstrations and processions in parks.
Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibited demonstrations and processions in places of worship.
Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibited demonstrations and processions in buildings in which public services were based.

Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) required that demonstrations organised in public squares comply with security instructions and not disrupt individuals' movement or public transport.

Section 24 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provided that demonstrations and processions which did not comply with the provisions of the Act would be dispersed by force on the order of the governor's office and after the demonstrators had been warned.

According to the circular issued by the Governorship of Ankara on 18 December 2000, which provides guidelines on meetings and demonstrations, Kızılay avenue is not among the permitted areas for demonstrations.
Article 16(a) of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that the police may use firearms in the event of self-defence.

Article 16(h) of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that the police may use firearms if a person or a group resists the police and prevents them from carrying out their duties or if there is an attack against the police.

Additional Article 6 (dated 16 June 1985) of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that in cases of resistance by persons whose arrest is necessary or by groups whose dispersal is necessary, or of their threatening to attack or carrying out an attack, the police may use violence to subdue these actions.

Additional Article 6 (dated 16 June 1985) of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that use of violence refers to the use of bodily force, physical force and all types of weapons specified in the law, and it gradually increases according to the nature and level of resistance and attack in such a way as to restore calm.

Additional Article 6 (dated 16 June 1985) of Law no. 2559 on the Duties and Powers of the Police provides that in cases of intervention by group forces, the extent of the use of force and the equipment and instruments to be used are determined by the commander of the intervening force.

On 26 June 2001, the Ankara public prosecutor brought charges against twenty-seven demonstrators, including Arzu Doğan and Sami Evren, for violation of the Law on Meetings and Demonstration Marches (Law no. 2911).
On 9 October 2001, the Ministry of the Interior decided not to take action against the officials and officers accused by the applicants.
The Ministry of the Interior found that the allegations made by the applicants against the officials and officers were of an 'abstract nature'.
The Ministry of the Interior considered that the force used by the police during the incidents of 7 June 2001 and 25 June 2001 was lawful and justified in the circumstances of the case.
The Ministry of the Interior considered that the police officers had been under an obligation to disperse the demonstrators who had organised an illegal meeting.
In a decision of 14 November 2001, the Ankara Criminal Court acquitted Arzu Doğan of the charges brought against her for violation of the Law on Meetings and Demonstration Marches (Law no. 2911).
In a decision of 14 November 2001, the Ankara Criminal Court acquitted Sami Evren of the charges brought against him for violation of the Law on Meetings and Demonstration Marches (Law no. 2911).

In a decision of 14 November 2001, the Ankara Criminal Court acquitted other demonstrators of the charges brought against them for violation of the Law on Meetings and Demonstration Marches (Law no. 2911).
The Ankara Criminal Court decided in its decision of 14 November 2001 that the demonstrators enjoyed a right to hold unarmed and peaceful meetings and demonstrations without prior permission.

On 29 January 2002, the Ankara public prosecutor issued a decision of non-prosecution as regards the applicants' complaints against the Ankara Governor, the director of the Ankara Security Directorate, the director of the Rapid Intervention Force branch of the Ankara Security Directorate, and the police officers involved in the incidents.
